items.title: Carolyn Buck Interview, 1969-03-25
items.q: He said, and he doesn't like any remarks given out because there's no need for it. He knows the capability of some musicians that they can do had they not been in this condition. I mean, he liked Louie Nelson's playing.

ctx.x: Did George say anything about Bill Russell?

He said he's a living saint, always. And that's one person that whenever he came, George was asleep. If I had given him a shot for pain or for sleep, I always woke him up for that because I knew he wanted Issybill. Always. Even if it was just to look at him. Louie Nelson came in to see him. All of his sons came. No, all but one son came to see him. His two sons, by a former marriage, had come to see him. His daughter had not arrived, nor had his first wife arrived. The letter came, the second wife. And a few…
What about this? Can you describe the actual... Do you think you could see if you could keep them up?
